_comment: The author role's data, declared once. bootstrap.py builds the role's App
manifest from `required`, mint-token.sh checks every minted token against it,
`fallback` is what as-role.sh does when this role has no App configured:
"operator" runs the command as the operator's own account, "refuse" fails
it. The author falls back: on a forge or plan where a bot per role costs too
much, acting as the operator is the supported configuration.
`consequence` is printed to whoever hits a shortfall, so it is addressed to
them: what stops working, not why the permission exists.

why.contents: push branches; delete a merged branch
why.pull_requests: open PRs, edit their descriptions, mark them ready, reply to and resolve review threads
why.issues: claim issues, file them, edit their bodies, comment, label
why.statuses: combined commit status, for CI that posts statuses instead of check runs

consequence.contents: pushes from a worktree are refused
consequence.pull_requests: PRs cannot be opened, edited or marked ready, and review threads cannot be answered
consequence.issues: claims, filed issues, issue comments and body edits all fail
consequence.workflows: a push that changes a file under .github/workflows/ is refused
consequence.checks: check runs are invisible, so a red build reads as no build
consequence.actions: the rollup cannot dereference workflow runs
consequence.statuses: CI that posts commit statuses instead of check runs is invisible
